newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power extends gain on line limits.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power extends gain on line limits.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. extended recent gains Tuesday due to transmission limits in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, traders said.
Constraints on the system have divided PJM into two smaller systems, an eastern and a western section.

"The split system has something to do with it," said a PJM power trader when asked about today's price rise. He added expectations of a cold front hitting the Mid-Atlantic Wednesday also pushed up next-day electricity values.
Forecasts showed temperatures would average near normal Wednesday with a chance of light snow. A cold air mass is expected to push readings two to seven degrees F below normal Thursday and Friday.
Transmission restrictions in PJM, which began last week, were triggered by high import demand from eastern PJM for cheaper generation from the west.

A refueling outage at the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear unit in Pennsylvania further cut power flows eastward, forcing utilities to switch on expensive oil and natural gas generation to balance the grid if they should need to bring cheap, coal-fired power from the west.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Wednesday (excluding transmission costs) increased to $26.50-27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Monday's $25.50-26.25 for delivery today.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak delivery Wednesday widened to $16.00-18.00 from $16.00-17.00 Monday.
PJM power deliveries until end of February tightened to $26.50-27.00, compared with Monday's $26.00-27.00.
March PJM power prices widened to $23.80-24.10 from $23.80-24.00 Monday.
PJM prices for April and May edged down to $21.80-21.90 from $21.90-22.00 Monday while June PJM power continued to hold at $24.75-25.00.
July/August PJM power slid to $29.70-29.75 from Monday's $29.80-30.00.
PJM third-quarter quotes fell to $27.55-27.55 from $27.80-28.00 Monday. and fourth-quarter PJM prices slipped to $23.70-23.80 from Monday's range of $23.85-24.00.
Firm, peak 1998 PJM deliveries softened to $25.75-25.95, from a quote of $25.95 Monday.
Separately, a 600 MW Homer City, Pa., coal-fired unit is resumed service late Monday after being taken off line last Thursday to repair a flame scanner.
Swing natural gas at the Philadelphia city gate was valued at $2.75-2.90 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) versus Monday's notional range at $2.75-3.00.
As of 1237 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures were up 1.8 cents at $2.185/mmBtu.
